svg.title: Railway Assistant Bot – Refactored HLD
svg.desc: Three-column HLD with refactored LangGraph: guardrail, intent classifier, planner, router, orchestrator, responder, logger nodes. Application layer has middleware above FastAPI. Data layer has PostgreSQL, external APIs, and Qdrant.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What does the Streamlit frontend handle?')
sendPrompt('What does auth middleware do and why does it not appear inside LangGraph?')
sendPrompt('What does FastAPI route and what is the difference between /chat and the REST endpoints?')
sendPrompt('What do the REST endpoints do directly against PostgreSQL?')
sendPrompt('What attack types does the guardrail node detect and what happens on a safe vs attack classification?')
sendPrompt('How does the intent classifier produce multiple intents with confidence scores and why does it not call any APIs or DB?')
sendPrompt('How does the planner resolve conflicts between multiple intents and generate an ordered execution plan?')
sendPrompt('What does the Router node do and why does it have no side effects — no DB or API calls?')
g.text: Maps plan steps to execution paths

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What are all the side effects the Orchestrator handles — DB reads and writes, external API calls, and Qdrant RAG retrieval?')
sendPrompt('What does the Responder node do with the collected results to generate the final reply?')
sendPrompt('What does the Logger node persist and why is persistence isolated to this node only?')
sendPrompt('What does the safe fallback response say when the guardrail detects an attack?')
sendPrompt('What tables does PostgreSQL hold for the Railway Assistant?')
sendPrompt('Which external APIs does the orchestrator call?')
sendPrompt('What does Qdrant store and how does the orchestrator use it for RAG?')
sendPrompt('How do REST endpoints write directly to PostgreSQL without going through LangGraph?')

svg.text: guardrail → classify · classifier → detect · planner → plan · router → route · orchestrator → execute · logger → persist
